clue.text: In theatre, it depends on support doctor gets with work

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A theatre production relies on a backer and a doctor joining in the work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depends' is used in its old sense of 'hangs down': a backdrop is the painted cloth hanging at the back of a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A painted cloth hung at the rear of a stage is literally suspended there, which is the old meaning of depending.

clue.text: Effect a letter from abroad produced on first lady

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so foreign to English
Eve is the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A foreign letter turns up from the President's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' suggests a president's wife, but here it is the biblical first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To effect something is to bring it about, to accomplish or attain it.

clue.text: Centrepiece manufacturer in Warwick?

parts.note: the king is the central piece of a chess game, the one the game revolves around
a maker is one who manufactures things

explanation.surface: A table centrepiece is made in the Midlands town of Warwick.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Neville, Earl of Warwick, was nicknamed this for his role in putting kings on the English throne during the Wars of the Roses; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth-century Earl of Warwick earned this nickname by deposing and installing monarchs.

clue.text: Summary removal of head of venture

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym for venture is taken away

parts.note: to venture a remark is to presume to make it

explanation.surface: A brief report on the beheading of a business venture.
explanation.walkthrough: The synonym PRESUME loses its first letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: A résumé is a short account summing up the main points.

clue.text: Accelerated and sped out of town on trip

indicators.note: a trip, like a stumble or a drug-induced one, throws these letters into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone drove fast as they set off from town on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' reads as the journey but is the anagram signal; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing the pedal hard to the floor is the idiom for driving faster.

clue.text: Support religious leader needed in divided church

indicators.note: the first letter of religious is required inside the divided church pair

parts.note: something divided has been cut

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A religious leader is needed to support a church split by schism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divided church' reads as a church in schism, but 'divided' supplies its own synonym ahead of the church abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A crutch is a prop, literal or figurative, that holds someone up.

clue.text: Concerned to keep temper, being reprimanded

indicators.note: the word for concerned holds the word for temper inside it

parts.note: to have cared is to have been concerned
a pet is a fit of bad temper or sulking

explanation.surface: A worried person tries to keep their temper while being told off.
explanation.definitionFit: To be carpeted is to be summoned before a superior for a scolding, originally on the boss's carpet.

clue.text: Period in school — fashionable one providing last places to train?

parts.note: a school year is split into terms
in means trendy or fashionable
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A school term spent being trendy prepares someone for their final training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train' looks like a verb about education; it is the railway sort.
explanation.definitionFit: End stations of a railway line are where trains finish their journeys.

clue.text: Indecision putting the case in disarray

indicators.note: letters in disarray are jumbled out of their original order

explanation.surface: Being unable to decide leaves a legal case in a mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitation or wavering is a failure to make up one's mind.

clue.text: Complains as hard drinks get passed around

indicators.note: the drinks go round the abbreviation for hard, enclosing it

parts.note: wines are drinks
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles as stiff drinks are handed round the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passed around' looks like serving drinks; it puts WINES around H.
explanation.definitionFit: To whine is to grumble in a peevish, nagging way.

clue.text: Agonies created by wrong sure to be settled

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

indicators.note: the letters of the word sure are settled into a new order

explanation.surface: Pain is caused by a legal wrong that is sure to be resolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be settled' rearranges SURE into URES.
explanation.definitionFit: Torture is extreme suffering, so the plural matches agonies.

clue.text: Course directors giving old protective headgear to soldiers

parts.note: helm is an archaic word for a helmet
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Antique helmets are handed out to troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' sounds like a lesson series or golf, but it is a ship's course.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who steer a vessel decide the direction it sails.

clue.text: It goes wrong for self-serving type

indicators.note: something gone wrong is out of its proper order

explanation.surface: Things go wrong for a selfish person.
explanation.definitionFit: An egoist puts personal interest above everyone else's.

clue.text: Makes impact with bills in large numbers

definitions.meaning: birds strike with their beaks, or bills
a peck is an old measure, used informally for a great many

explanation.surface: A company hit hard by invoices arriving in great quantity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bills' suggests invoices; it means beaks. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds jab with their beaks; a peck of trouble means plenty of it.

clue.text: Female creature, thanks to weight gain, displays figure that's magic!

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
ta is British informal for thank you
a gram is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A female animal, after putting on weight, shows off an amazing figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' suggests a body shape; it is a geometric figure used in magic.
explanation.definitionFit: The five-pointed star is a shape long used as a symbol in occult ritual.

clue.text: Slander like a catty type, we hear

indicators.note: this signals the words are spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: as means like, and a Persian is a breed of cat

explanation.surface: Spiteful gossip sounds like the talk of a catty person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catty type' suggests a spiteful person, but it is literally a Persian cat; 'as Persian' spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Casting aspersions means making damaging, untrue remarks about someone.

clue.text: Newspaper proprietor entertaining large number for evening drink

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to take them in, so these words enclose the number

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily newspaper
a proprietor is an owner
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A press baron hosts a big crowd for drinks in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink taken at sunset is the colonial-era name for an evening tipple.

clue.text: Way to encourage a swimmer

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: A method of cheering on someone in a swimming race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' suggests a person; it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This large fish, source of caviar, is a creature that swims.

clue.text: Managed returns to share account

indicators.note: returns means the word for managed is read backwards

parts.note: to have run something is to have managed it
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: Someone who ran a business returns to give a financial report.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling a story or giving an account of events is narration.

clue.text: Eastern friend casually displaying Polish

indicators.note: done casually, the letters fall into a loose new order

explanation.surface: A friend from the East casually shows off Polish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' masquerades as the nationality thanks to its capital; it means polish, refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cultured and elegant shows the polish of good manners.

clue.text: Mounties to some extent set free

indicators.note: only part of the word Mounties is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Canadian police release someone, after a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten a knot or bonds is to release.

clue.text: Popular one-time performer, not altogether nice

parts.note: in means popular
ex means former, and an act is a performer or turn

explanation.surface: A famous former entertainer is not entirely pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nice' is used in its sense of precise, as in a nice distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice can mean precise or exact, so not quite nice is imprecise.

clue.text: Prize initially given to runner-up in introductory test

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word prize
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a miler is a runner over a mile

explanation.surface: A prize goes to the second-placed finisher in a qualifying race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner-up' looks like the second placed; it is a runner plus a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary examination, shortened colloquially, is an introductory exam.

clue.text: Liaison in business

definitions.meaning: a liaison is a romantic or sexual relationship
a business is a matter or concern, as in 'that's my business'

explanation.surface: A romantic liaison at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a love affair and a matter of concern share this word.

clue.text: Pass on responsibility for the takings

definitions.meaning: to turn something over to someone is to hand it to them
a firm's gross income over a period

explanation.surface: Handing over responsibility for the day's receipts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Handing over is turning over; a company's sales income is its turnover.

clue.text: American stockman escaped with chore undone

parts.note: ran means fled or escaped

indicators.note: undone means taken apart, so the letters of chore are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cowboy ran off with his chores left unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undone' rearranges CHORE into CHERO.
explanation.definitionFit: In the American south-west a rancher or ranch hand is called a ranchero.

clue.text: Transport to bring gold ashore

parts.note: ashore means on land
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A ship carries gold to be unloaded on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring' is a link; read 'bring gold ashore' as gold placed after the land word.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, a means of transport.

clue.text: Course set by sailors in current

parts.note: a mode is a course or manner of action
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

explanation.surface: A course plotted by sailors in a sea current.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like a flow of water; it means present-day. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something up to date belongs to the present time.

clue.text: Able to calculate tax on source of earnings by miners

parts.note: the NUM is Britain's National Union of Mineworkers

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a rate is a local tax

explanation.surface: Miners' union seeks a tax on the basis of their earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: Being competent with numbers and arithmetic is the counterpart of literate.
